# jackie-brain-twin

**Digital twin of the canine subject “Jackie” (Canis lupus familiaris)**  
Reconstructed from multi-session functional MRI, simultaneous EEG, physiological telemetry and behavioural annotation.

![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)
![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.9%2B-blue)
![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-research%20prototype-orange)

---

## Table of Contents

1. [Project Summary](#project-summary)
2. [Scientific Background](#scientific-background)
3. [Included fMRI Slices](#included-fmri-slices)
4. [Repository Layout](#repository-layout)
5. [Data Description](#data-description)
6. [Installation](#installation)
7. [Quick Start](#quick-start)
8. [Interactive Commands](#interactive-commands)
9. [Core Architecture](#core-architecture)
10. [Emotion & Region Dynamics](#emotion--region-dynamics)
11. [Extending the Model](#extending-the-model)
12. [Reproducibility Notes](#reproducibility-notes)
13. [Limitations](#limitations)
14. [Citation](#citation)
15. [License](#license)

---

## Project Summary

`jackie-brain-twin` is a modular Python framework that reconstructs the real-time emotional and regional brain state of a single dog (Jackie) from actual neuroimaging and physiological recordings.  

The system ingests:

- Six fully annotated scan sessions (J001–J006) containing BOLD values for olfactory bulbs, amygdalae and nucleus accumbens, EEG band-power percentages, heart rate, respiration, acceleration and behavioural markers.
- Three high-resolution axial fMRI slices acquired under distinct social conditions (novel street dog, highly familiar best-friend dog, and a neighbor dog after repeated exposure).

From these data the model continuously updates a six-dimensional emotional vector (joy, curiosity, calm, excitement, anxiety, affection) and a 25-region activation map. The resulting digital twin can be queried with arbitrary textual stimuli and returns an interpretable state vector together with the most probable behavioural phenotype.

---

## Scientific Background

Dogs possess an expanded olfactory system and a well-developed social brain network. The present reconstruction focuses on three key nodes repeatedly implicated in canine social neuroscience:

- **Olfactory bulbs** – primary sensory gate for conspecific and environmental odours  
- **Amygdala** – rapid valence and threat evaluation  
- **Nucleus accumbens** – reward and social motivation  

Additional regions (cingulate, temporal pole, superior temporal gyrus, prefrontal areas, etc.) are maintained at baseline and modulated by derived regression weights.  

All numeric values in `scan_data.py` are taken directly from the original recording sessions; no synthetic data were introduced for the six core sessions. The three axial slices serve as visual ground-truth for the social-stimulus conditions.

---

## Included fMRI Slices

Three axial T2*-weighted EPI slices are provided in the `assets/` directory.  
Acquisition parameters common to all three:

- Sequence: T2*-weighted gradient-echo EPI  
- TR / TE: 2000 ms / 30 ms  
- Slice thickness: 2.0 mm  
- In-plane resolution: ≈ 1.2 × 1.2 mm  
- Subject: Canis lupus familiaris (Jackie)

| Condition              | File name                                      | Heart Rate | Key activation pattern                          | Notes |
|------------------------|------------------------------------------------|------------|------------------------------------------------|-------|
| Random street dog      | `assets/image - 2026-10-14T115850.011.jpg`     | 124 bpm    | Bilateral amygdala + olfactory overlay         | Novel social stimulus, elevated arousal |
| Best friend dog        | `assets/image - 2026-10-14T115911.524.jpg`     | 112 bpm    | Focal mid-brain / thalamic and temporal foci   | Highly familiar conspecific, balanced response |
| Neighbor dog           | `assets/image - 2026-10-14T115921.681.jpg`     | 98 bpm     | Strong bilateral temporal-lobe activation      | Later exposure session, reduced autonomic load |

**Random street dog** (novel, high arousal)  
![Random street dog](assets/image%20-%202026-10-14T115850.011.jpg)

**Best friend dog** (highly familiar)  
![Best friend dog](assets/image%20-%202026-10-14T115911.524.jpg)

**Neighbor dog** (now familiar)  
![Neighbor dog](assets/image%20-%202026-10-14T115921.681.jpg)

---


## Emotion & Region DynamicsDecay 

every region exponentially relaxes toward its anatomical baseline (DECAY_RATE = 0.927).
Injection – BOLD values from a matched session are scaled by intensity and added to the corresponding regions.
Social boosts – hard-coded additive offsets for the three social conditions (see config.REGION_BOOST).
Emotional regression – stimulus-to-emotion weights were derived by averaging the six real sessions and centring around zero; the resulting linear mapping is stored in JackieCore.mappings.

## Reproducibility NotesAll 
floating-point values in the six core sessions are taken verbatim from the original recording logs.
Random number generation is used only for demonstration ordering and for unknown-stimulus jitter; seeding is not required for deterministic replay of the recorded sessions.
The three fMRI JPEGs are the exact axial slices acquired during the corresponding social runs.



## Data Description

### Session table (excerpt)

| SID  | Stimulus                     | Duration | Intensity | HR  | Olf L/R BOLD | Amyg L/R BOLD | NAcc L/R BOLD | Confidence |
|------|------------------------------|----------|-----------|-----|--------------|---------------|---------------|------------|
| J001 | chicken meat                 | 300 s    | high      | 118 | 1.82 / 1.28  | 2.40 / 2.21   | 2.21 / 4.31   | 0.89       |
| J002 | best friend dog              | 300 s    | high      | 112 | 1.36 / 1.68  | 0.92 / 0.88   | 1.55 / 1.42   | 0.83       |
| J003 | random street dog            | 300 s    | medium    | 126 | 0.65 / 0.72  | 0.35 / 0.41   | 0.52 / 0.48   | 0.61       |
| J004 | walk                         | 600 s    | low       | 104 | 0.12 / 0.18  | –0.05 / 0.02  | 0.10 / 0.08   | 0.72       |
| J005 | first exposure neighbor dog  | 300 s    | medium    | 121 | 0.78 / 0.95  | 0.48 / 0.55   | 0.68 / 0.71   | 0.64       |
| J006 | later session neighbor dog   | 300 s    | high      | 115 | 1.25 / 1.49  | 0.85 / 0.79   | 1.12 / 1.05   | 0.81       |

Full numeric vectors (EEG band percentages, z-scores, acceleration, licking, etc.) are stored as `Session` dataclasses inside `scan_data.py`.

---
Example session:
> best friend dog
#42 best friend dog → affection  HR=112.0  arousal=0.412  {'joy': 0.61, ...}

> i 1.6 random street dog
#43 random street dog → anxiety  HR=124.0  arousal=0.783  ...

> social
random street dog     → anxiety    HR=124  fMRI=assets/image - 2026-10-14T115850.011.jpg
best friend dog       → affection  HR=112  fMRI=assets/image - 2026-10-14T115911.524.jpg
neighbor dog          → calm       HR=98   fMRI=assets/image - 2026-10-14T115921.681.jpg
## Installation

```bash
git clone https://github.com/<your-username>/jackie-brain-twin.git
cd jackie-brain-twin
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate          # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -r requirements.txt    # currently only stdlib required

items.readme:
House Control

Your home as a live 3D model — in the Mac's menu bar, around its notch and on your iPhone —
controlling its lights and air conditioners through Smart Life, Home Assistant, Philips Hue and Apple Home.

Download  ·  Build it yourself  ·  Support the project

## What it does - **Lives in the menu bar.** Click the house icon and a panel drops down; click anywhere else and it is gone. - **Your floor plan in 3D.** Rooms, walls, doors, windows and furniture are built from one JSON file. Lamps light the scene the way they light the room; an AC that is running blows visible air. - **Lights.** Tap to toggle, drag across a tile to dim, open a light for brightness, white temperature and colour. - **Air conditioners.** Power, target temperature, mode and fan speed, with the room temperature from a real sensor if you have one. - **Scenes.** One tap sets every light and AC — "Cozy", "Movie", "Night", or your own. - **A visual editor.** Draw the rooms, drop in furniture, place lamps and ACs, and link each one to a real device. - **Your devices, wherever they live.** Smart Life / Tuya, Home Assistant (and the thousands of brands it runs), Philips Hue and Apple Home — mixed freely in one home. See [Connect real devices](#connect-real-devices). - **An island around the notch.** Rest the pointer on the MacBook's notch and a small live model of the home drops out of it, with scenes and every device one click away. See [The island](#the-island). - **AI Access.** Give ChatGPT, Claude or any AI assistant a private link — or connect it over MCP — and it runs your lights and air conditioners, and rebuilds rooms in the 3D model from your photos. Served by your Mac; Stop ends it. See [AI Access](#ai-access). - **An iPhone app.** The same home in your pocket, kept in sync with the Mac over your own Wi-Fi. See [iPhone app](#iphone-app). - **Works without any hardware.** Until you sign in, every device is simulated, so you can try everything first. Both apps are a small native Swift shell (AppKit on the Mac, SwiftUI on the iPhone) around one [Three.js](https://threejs.org) web UI, and share their device clients and sync as a Swift package. No frameworks, no Electron, no server, no account of its own. ## Download 1. Get `HouseControl-.dmg` from [Releases](https://github.com/0xProbabillity/house-control/releases). It runs on macOS 13 or newer, Apple silicon and Intel. 2. Open it and drag **House Control** into **Applications**. 3. Open **House Control** from Applications. The first time, macOS stops it with *“Apple could not verify…”*, because the app is not signed with a paid Apple Developer ID (see [why](#why-the-app-is-not-notarized)). Allow it once: - **macOS 15 Sequoia and newer:** click **Done**, open **System Settings → Privacy & Security**, scroll down to *“House Control was blocked…”*, click **Open Anyway** and confirm with your password. - **macOS 13–14:** Control-click the app in Applications, choose **Open**, then **Open** again. - Or, in Terminal: `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/House Control.app"` 4. Look for the house in the menu bar — there is no Dock icon and no window. Click it. It starts with a bundled demo plan, so you can try everything before connecting anything. Then: [make it your home](#make-it-your-home) and [connect real devices](#connect-real-devices). To start it with your Mac, add it under **System Settings → General → Login Items**. ### Check what you downloaded Every release image is built by [GitHub Actions](.github/workflows/release.yml) from the tagged commit — not on anyone's Mac — and comes with its SHA-256 and a signed build provenance attestation: ```bash shasum -a 256 -c HouseControl-.dmg.sha256 gh attestation verify HouseControl-.dmg --repo 0xProbabillity/house-control ``` The second command proves the image was built by this repository's workflow, and shows from which commit. ### Why the app is not notarized Notarizing needs an Apple Developer ID, and that certificate carries a person's legal name inside every copy of the app. House Control ships signed ad hoc instead, and earns trust the open-source way: the code is all here, the release is built in public, and you can [build it yourself](#build-and-run) in a couple of minutes. ### Remove it Quit it (right-click the menu bar icon → **Quit**), delete **House Control** from Applications and, to remove your plan and connections too, `~/Library/Application Support/HouseControl/`. ## Requirements | | | | --- | --- | | macOS | 13 Ventura or newer | | Xcode Command Line Tools | Swift 5.9 or newer — `xcode-select --install` | | Node.js | 20.19+ or 22.12+ | | For the iPhone app | Xcode 16 or newer, [XcodeGen](https://github.com/yonaskolb/XcodeGen) (`brew install xcodegen`), iOS 17+ | ## Build and run ```bash git clone https://github.com/0xProbabillity/house-control.git cd house-control ./scripts/build-app.sh open build/HouseControl.app ``` The script builds the web UI with Vite, the native shell with SwiftPM, and assembles an ad-hoc signed `build/HouseControl.app`. The first build downloads the npm packages; later builds take a few seconds. The app is signed ad hoc. If you rebuild often and use iPhone sync, sign it with your own certificate instead, so macOS does not ask for the Local Network permission after every build: `CODESIGN_IDENTITY="Apple Development: you@example.com (ABCDE12345)" ./scripts/build-app.sh`. To keep it, drag `build/HouseControl.app` into `/Applications`. To start it with your Mac, add it under **System Settings → General → Login Items**. There is no Dock icon and no main window: look for the house in the menu bar. ## Using it | Do this | To get this | | --- | --- | | Click the menu bar icon | Open or close the panel | | Right-click the menu bar icon | Edit Home, Load Floor Plan, Reveal Plan File, Reveal Device Log, Show Island, Pair iPhone, AI Access, Reload, Quit | | Click a lamp in the 3D view, or its tile | Toggle it | | Drag sideways across a light tile | Dim it | | Click the sliders icon on a light tile | Brightness, white temperature, colour | | Click an AC, or its tile | Open its sheet: temperature, mode, fan speed | | Click a room | Zoom in on it and list only its devices | | Drag the 3D view / scroll over it | Rotate / zoom | | `Esc` | Back, then close | The menu bar icon shows how many lights are on and the target of the running AC, for example `6 · 23°`. The gear button in the panel switches between your home and the two bundled demo plans, **Apartment** and **Studio**. ## The island

A black tab grows out of the MacBook's notch. On a display without a notch it is drawn in the middle of the menu bar. | Do this | To get this | | --- | --- | | Look at it | How many lights are on, and the target of a running AC | | Rest the pointer on it | It springs open: the 3D model, scenes, air conditioners and lights | | Click a lamp in the model, or its chip | Toggle it; drag across a chip to dim | | Click a room in the model | Zoom in on it | | Move the pointer away | It closes | When something changes elsewhere — a scene picked in the panel, a lamp switched from the phone — the island peeks out for a moment to say what happened. It never takes the keyboard from the app you are working in. **Show Island** in the menu bar icon's right-click menu turns it off. ## AI Access

Right-click the menu bar icon → **AI Access…** → **Start AI Access**, and hand the private link to an assistant: - **Any chat:** paste it into ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or Perplexity with your request — *"dim the living room to 30%"*. The link opens a guide written for AI assistants, with an action link for everything it can do. - **Connectors:** add the MCP address as a custom connector in Claude or ChatGPT (or `claude mcp add` in Claude Code) and the assistant can also change the home itself: *"here are photos of my living room — rebuild it in 3D"*. - **Your own agents:** the same tools as plain HTTP + JSON, with an OpenAPI description. The Mac serves it all: House Control listens on `127.0.0.1` only and is reached through a Cloudflare quick tunnel that exists while AI Access is on (or not at all, with **This Mac only**). The link carries a 128-bit key, you choose what an assistant may do, every request shows up live in the window, plan edits can be undone, and **Stop** — or the auto-stop timer — makes the address disappear. Device IDs and sign-ins never leave the Mac. Details, every tool, and the privacy model: [docs/ai-access.md](docs/ai-access.md). ## iPhone app

The iPhone app is the panel made for a thumb: tap a lamp in the 3D view or its tile, drag across a tile to dim, touch and hold a light for brightness and colour, pinch the model to zoom, swipe in from the left edge to go back. Try it in the simulator: ```bash ./scripts/ios-sim.sh ``` To put it on a phone, write your Apple developer team into `ios/Config/Local.xcconfig` (`DEVELOPMENT_TEAM = ABCDE12345`), run `cd ios && xcodegen generate`, open `ios/HouseControl.xcodeproj` and run it on your device. `./scripts/build-ios.sh --upload` archives it and sends it to TestFlight; the script lists what it needs. ### Sync with the Mac Your floor plan — rooms, furniture, lamps, scenes and the links to real devices — is drawn on the Mac and travels to the phone by itself. 1. On the Mac: right-click the menu bar icon → **Pair iPhone…**. A QR code appears. macOS asks once whether House Control may find devices on your local network: allow it. 2. On the iPhone: **Settings** (the sliders button) → **Pair with Mac**, and point the camera at the code. Or press **Copy Pairing Link** on the Mac and paste it on the phone. From then on, whenever both are on the same Wi-Fi and the app is open, the phone has what the Mac has: **Save & apply** in the editor updates the phone a moment later. Nothing goes through a server. The Mac advertises itself with Bonjour and the two talk over TLS with a pre-shared key that only the QR code carries, so a device that never saw the code cannot connect. **Reset Pairing…** in the pairing window issues a new key. ### Real devices on the iPhone The phone signs in to Smart Life on its own: **Settings → Connect Smart Life**. The User Code is filled in from the Mac if you are signed in there. The sign-in code has to be scanned by the Smart Life app, which is on the very phone you are holding — so the paired Mac puts the code on its screen for you. Without a Mac, share the code to any other screen. The session is kept in the iPhone's Keychain and never leaves the device. ## Make it your home Right-click the icon and choose **Edit Home…**

- Drag rooms to move them and drag a corner to resize; everything snaps to 5 cm. - Where two rooms touch, the wall between them appears by itself. Walls facing the camera are cut away. - Add doors, windows, furniture, lamps and air conditioners from the list on the left. - **Save & apply** writes the plan and reloads the panel. The plan is a single JSON file, `~/Library/Application Support/HouseControl/plan.json`. You can write it by hand, export it, or import someone else's: see [docs/floor-plan.md](docs/floor-plan.md) for every field. The demo plans in [`web/public/plans`](web/public/plans) are good starting points. ## Connect real devices

Right-click the icon → **Edit Home… → Connections**, and connect what you have: | Platform | How | Details | | --- | --- | --- | | **Smart Life / Tuya** | Scan a QR code with the Smart Life app. No Tuya developer account | [docs/smart-life.md](docs/smart-life.md) | | **Home Assistant** | Found on your network by itself; paste a long-lived access token | [docs/connections.md](docs/connections.md#home-assistant) | | **Philips Hue** | Found on your network by itself; press the button on the bridge | [docs/connections.md](docs/connections.md#philips-hue) | | **Apple Home** | Allow access on your iPhone; its devices are listed on the Mac for linking | [docs/connections.md](docs/connections.md#apple-home) | Then select a lamp or an AC on the plan, choose its device under **Real device** (lamps take over what the device can do), and press **Save & apply**. From then on the panel controls the real device. Changes made elsewhere show up at once from Home Assistant and Hue, and within 12 seconds from Smart Life. Your iPhone receives the Home Assistant and Hue connections from the Mac with the floor plan, and switches Apple Home devices itself. Why there is no Google Home or Alexa yet, and how to get Tuya devices into Apple Home: [docs/connections.md](docs/connections.md). No hardware at hand? [`tools/lab`](tools/lab/README.md) has pretend versions of Home Assistant, a Hue Bridge and a HomeKit bridge. ## Privacy House Control talks to the platforms you connect — Tuya's servers for Smart Life, your own Home Assistant, your Hue Bridge, Apple Home on the iPhone — and to nothing else. There is no telemetry and no backend of its own. The one exception is yours to switch on: [AI Access](#ai-access) opens a Cloudflare tunnel to your Mac while it is on. Everything personal stays in `~/Library/Application Support/HouseControl/` on your Mac: | File | Contents | | --- | --- | | `plan.json` | Your floor plan, including the IDs of the devices you linked | | `settings.json` | Which plan is active | | `smartlife.json` | The Smart Life session tokens. Readable only by you (mode `600`) | | `tuya.json` | Tuya Cloud project credentials, only if you use that option. Mode `600` | | `homeassistant.json` | Your Home Assistant's address and access token. Mode `600` | | `hue.json` | Your Hue Bridge's address, the key it issued and its certificate's fingerprint. Mode `600` | | `homekit-devices.json` | The Apple Home devices your iPhone listed for the editor: names and ids | | `events.log` | Commands sent to real devices and the cloud's answers. No tokens | | `sync.json` | The key your paired iPhones use. Only there once you paired one. Mode `600` | | `cloudflared.yml`, `bin/cloudflared` | An empty config for AI Access's tunnel, and Cloudflare's connector if you let the app download it | None of these are part of this repository, and the build does not embed them in the app. **Sign out** in the editor deletes `smartlife.json`. Deleting the folder resets the app to the demo plan. On the iPhone the floor plan lives in the app's own folder, and the Smart Life session, the pairing key and the Home Assistant and Hue connections the Mac shared in the Keychain. ## Development ``` web/ the UI: Three.js scene, panel, island, editor, AI Access window and the AI tools (Vite, plain ES modules) core/ what both apps share: Smart Life and Tuya clients, plan store, Mac ⇄ iPhone sync, the AI gateway (SwiftPM, with tests) macos/ the Mac shell: menu bar item, panel, island and editor windows (SwiftPM) ios/ the iPhone shell: SwiftUI, generated into an Xcode project by XcodeGen scripts/ build-app.sh, build-ios.sh and ios-sim.sh build the apps, release-mac.sh makes the .dmg, make-icon.swift and make-dmg-background.swift draw the icon and the disk image's window tools/lab pretend Home Assistant, Hue Bridge and HomeKit bridge for testing without hardware docs/ floor plan reference, connection guides, screenshots ``` The shared package has unit tests, including the sync over a real TLS connection: ```bash cd core && swift test ``` Work on the UI in a browser with hot reload — the native bridge is a no-op there and all devices are simulated: ```bash cd web npm install npm run dev ``` Then open `http://localhost:5199/`. Add `?plan=studio` for the second demo plan, `?mode=editor` for the editor, `?mode=island` for the island, `?mode=agent` for the AI Access window (with a simulated link), `?platform=ios` for the iPhone layout, or `?device=living.ac` to start on a device's sheet. Set `PORT` to use another port. Environment variables understood by the app: | Variable | Effect | | --- | --- | | `HOUSE_DEV_URL=http://localhost:5199/` | Load the UI from the dev server instead of the bundle | | `HOUSE_WEB_DIR=/path/to/dist` | Load the UI from another folder | | `HOUSE_DATA_DIR=/some/folder` | Keep plan, session and log there instead of Application Support, and do not persist panel state. Handy for a clean test run | | `HOUSE_OPEN_ON_LAUNCH=1` | Open the panel at launch | | `HOUSE_OPEN_EDITOR=1` | Open the editor at launch (`connections`, `smartlife`, `homeassistant`, `hue` or `homekit` opens it on that screen) | | `HOUSE_OPEN_DEVICE=` | Start the panel on that light's or AC's sheet | | `HOUSE_PIN=1` | Keep the panel open when it loses focus | | `HOUSE_DOCK=1` | Show a Dock icon, so UI automation tools can see the app | | `HOUSE_ISLAND=0` | Run without the island (`1` forces it on) | | `HOUSE_ISLAND_EXPANDED=1` | Keep the island open | | `HOUSE_OPEN_PAIRING=1` | Open the Pair iPhone window at launch | | `HOUSE_COMPUTER_NAME="Studio Mac"` | The name paired iPhones see, instead of the Mac's own (screenshots) | | `HOUSE_SNAPSHOT_DIR=/some/folder` | Write `panel.png` and `island.png` there a few seconds after launch | | `HOUSE_RENDER_HIDDEN=1` | Keep drawing while the screen is locked, for unattended captures | | `HOUSE_OPEN_AGENT=1` | Open the AI Access window at launch (`start` also starts the link) | | `HOUSE_AGENT_REACH=local` | Serve AI Access on this Mac only for one run (`internet` for the tunnel) | | `HOUSE_AGENT_LINK_FILE=/some/file` | Write the live AI Access link there, for scripted tests | | `HOUSE_EVAL_DIR=/some/folder` | Scripted UI checks: a `panel.js` / `editor.js` / `island.js` dropped there runs in that page (as an async function body) and its result is written to `.json` | The iPhone app understands `HOUSE_DATA_DIR`, `HOUSE_OPEN_DEVICE` and `HOUSE_SCREEN=home|settings|connections|pairing|smartlife|welcome`; `scripts/ios-sim.sh` passes any `HOUSE_*` variable on to the simulator. For example, a throw-away instance on the demo plan, pinned open: ```bash HOUSE_DATA_DIR=/tmp/house-demo HOUSE_PIN=1 HOUSE_OPEN_ON_LAUNCH=1 build/HouseControl.app/Contents/MacOS/HouseControl ``` The binary has a few offline self-checks and one read-only diagnostic: | Command | Prints | | --- | --- | | `HouseControl --selftest-mapper` | The Tuya commands built for typical light and AC actions | | `HouseControl --selftest-infrared` | The key presses sent to an infrared AC, against a simulated cloud remote | | `HouseControl --selftest-transport` | The Smart Life request envelope for fixed inputs, to compare with the reference SDK | | `HouseControl --diagnose …` | What Smart Life reports for those devices. Reads only; sends nothing | ### Releasing the Mac app Set `MARKETING_VERSION` in `ios/Config/Base.xcconfig`, commit, then tag and push: ```bash git tag v0.1.0 && git push origin v0.1.0 ``` [`release.yml`](.github/workflows/release.yml) builds the universal app on a GitHub macOS runner (`UNSIGNED=1 ./scripts/release-mac.sh`), attests its provenance and opens a **draft** release with the disk image and its SHA-256. Check it, then publish the draft. Running the workflow by hand from the Actions tab builds the same image as a downloadable artifact without a release. With an Apple Developer ID of your own, `ASC_KEY_ID=… ASC_ISSUER_ID=… ./scripts/release-mac.sh --publish` builds a signed and notarized image locally instead; the script lists what it needs. ## Limitations - The iPhone app is not on the App Store (it is on TestFlight for the author's testers). - The floor plan is edited on the Mac only. The iPhone receives it, and only while both are on the same network. - Rooms are axis-aligned rectangles. An L-shaped room is two rooms. - Apple Home devices are switched by the iPhone app only: macOS gives HomeKit to App Store apps only. - Smart Life devices are reached through Tuya's cloud, not over the local network, so they need an internet connection (Home Assistant and Hue work on your network alone). - Infrared air conditioners are one-way: the app shows what was last sent, not what the unit is doing. ## Support the project House Control is free and has no ads. If it earned a place in your menu bar, a tip in crypto helps it keep growing: more devices, more platforms, quicker fixes. Thank you! A star, a bug report or a pull request helps just as much. Scan a code with your wallet, or copy an address with the button in the corner of its box. > [!IMPORTANT] > Send each coin only over the network named next to its address. Coins sent over another network may be lost.
  Bitcoin
BTC · native SegWit (bech32) address ```text bc1q07hfz95crdalcrnywjavdpc4pdvllct83as5re ```
  Ethereum · Base · BNB Chain · Arbitrum
One address on all four networks · ETH, BNB, USDT, USDC and other tokens ```text 0x4ed3aF428e938a0CC8e60df86D714B4a7F0928F0 ```

## Acknowledgements and disclaimer The Smart Life sign-in is a Swift port of Tuya's open-source [`tuya-device-sharing-sdk`](https://github.com/tuya/tuya-device-sharing-sdk), the library behind the Tuya integration in Home Assistant, and identifies itself to Tuya the same way. The 3D view is built with [Three.js](https://threejs.org); the icons are from [Lucide](https://lucide.dev), the network logos under [Support the project](#support-the-project) from [Web3 Icons](https://github.com/0xa3k5/web3icons) (MIT). This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by Tuya, Smart Life or Home Assistant. It relies on an interface Tuya can change at any time. Use it at your own risk. ## License [MIT](LICENSE)

items.readme:
English · Русский

Your PS5 game store.
Back from the dead, rebuilt from its own binary, with every line of source in the open.

Install · Features · Updates · Troubleshooting · Build it yourself

> [!NOTE] > The original Overdrive project has been shut down so I decompiled the last released build, > recovered the complete source and rebuilt it.

## Features - **1,800+ games** to discover, with **Top rated**, **New releases** and a featured spotlight - **Browse the whole library** with filters, sorting, scores and download sizes at a glance - **Downloads straight to the console**, to internal storage or any USB drive, with live speed and storage stats - **Favorites**, **search** with an on-screen keyboard, and a **Files** page to see and clean up what's on your drives - **13 languages**: English, Deutsch, Español, Français, Português (Brasil), Русский, Bahasa Indonesia, 日本語, 简体中文, العربية, اردو, हिन्दी, বাংলা - **Updates itself**: a new version installs from the console, no PC needed - Made for the controller: L1 R1 to switch sections, ✕ to select, ○ to go back ## Install in four steps

### Before you start You need a **jailbroken PS5** running **[ShadowMount+](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus)**, the payload that installs `.exfat` images by itself. If ShadowMount+ shows its notification when the console starts, you are ready. You also need a **USB drive** and a **PC**.

**Download `Overdrive.exfat`** with the button above, or from the [latest release](https://github.com/MyLuxy/overdrive/releases/latest). It is the only file you need. Leave it as it is: don't unzip it and don't change the `.exfat` at the end of its name.
**Copy it onto a USB drive, inside a folder called `homebrew`.** Plug the drive into your PC, create a new folder named exactly `homebrew` (all lowercase) at the top level of the drive, and copy `Overdrive.exfat` into it: ```text USB drive └── homebrew └── Overdrive.exfat ``` The drive must be formatted as **exFAT**, which is how most drives come and what the PS5 reads.
**Plug the drive into the PS5.** ShadowMount+ checks for new files every few seconds: it finds Overdrive, mounts it and installs it, and a notification tells you when it's done. There is nothing to click.
**Open Overdrive from the home screen.** Look for this icon. Enjoy!
You can also use **any FTP client** to move the file onto the console's internal storage instead, again inside a `homebrew` folder: `/data/homebrew/Overdrive.exfat`. ## Updates You only install Overdrive by hand once. When a new version comes out, the app tells you by itself a few seconds after it opens: 1. A window shows the new version and what changed. Press **Install**. 2. Overdrive downloads the update, checks it and puts it in place of the old one. 3. When it's done, the app **closes itself**. Open it again and you are on the new version. The update needs about **600 MB free** on the drive that holds Overdrive. `update.zip` in each release is the package the app downloads for this; you never need it yourself. ## Support the project Overdrive is free and open source. If you enjoy it, sponsoring helps me keep it updated.

## Troubleshooting
Overdrive doesn't appear on the home screen
- Make sure **ShadowMount+ is running**: it shows a notification when it starts. - Check the folder: it must be called exactly `homebrew` and sit at the **top level** of the drive, not inside another folder. - Check the file still ends in **`.exfat`**. Some PCs hide extensions: a file renamed to `Overdrive.exfat.zip` or unzipped into a folder won't be found. - Give it a minute: ShadowMount+ waits until the file has finished copying before it installs it.
After an update, the app still shows the old version
The new version is installed but the console still has the old one loaded. **Restart the console** and open Overdrive again; the app tells you this itself if it happens twice in a row.
The update says there isn't enough space
The update is downloaded next to the installed app, so the drive holding Overdrive needs about 600 MB free. Free some space on that drive and press **Retry**. Nothing has been changed yet when this happens.
The update says it couldn't replace the app
Install it by hand: download `Overdrive.exfat` from the [latest release](https://github.com/MyLuxy/overdrive/releases/latest), close Overdrive, and copy the new file over the old one in the `homebrew` folder.
How do I remove Overdrive?
Delete `Overdrive.exfat` from the `homebrew` folder first, then delete its icon from the home screen. In the other order ShadowMount+ finds the file again and puts the icon back.
## Build it yourself
What's in this repository
| Path | What it is | | --- | --- | | `app/` | The application: JSX sources, state, assets, catalog data, and `app.json` (title id `PPSA99058`, version, capabilities) | | `ps5-react/` | The framework it runs on, vendored from [half144/ps5-react](https://github.com/half144/ps5-react) | | `packaging/make-exfat.sh` | Builds the exFAT image ShadowMount+ installs | | `.github/workflows/build.yml` | The build |
How the source was recovered
Overdrive is a React app running on [ps5-react](https://github.com/half144/ps5-react), and its whole JavaScript bundle sits in plain text inside `eboot.bin`. A bundler merges every module into one scope, so imports between modules turn into bare names; since each top-level name stays unique, the module that declares a name can be worked out again. That split the bundle back into its 137 original modules with their real `import`/`export` lines, checked against the original bundle until every import edge matched. What a bundler throws away could not come back: most comments, the JSX syntax (it reads as `jsx(View, {…})` calls), and `const`/`let` (now `var`). None of that changes how the app behaves.
Building
Builds run on `ubuntu-24.04` with clang 18, only from **Run workflow**: a push builds nothing. Each run puts `Overdrive.exfat` and `update.zip` in a draft release named after `app/version.js`, which only maintainers can see. The same build locally, on any Linux with the packages the workflow installs (`clang-18`, `llvm-18`, `cmake`, `ninja-build`, `nodejs`, `npm`, `zlib1g-dev`, `build-essential`, `pkg-config`, `unzip`, `curl`, `exfatprogs`, and Pillow from `ps5-react/requirements.txt`): ```sh cd ps5-react python3 tools/build_ps5.py --app-dir ../app --llvm /usr/bin sudo ../packaging/make-exfat.sh dist/PPSA99058 ../Overdrive.exfat ``` The build downloads its pinned dependencies into `ps5-react/.deps` and writes the app folder, a `.zip` and a `.receipt.json` into `ps5-react/dist`. It verifies the result itself (`tools/verify.py`), so a green build means the payload structure and signatures check out. `--llvm /usr/bin` points it at the system clang; upstream defaults to the Homebrew LLVM path because macOS is its supported development environment. The image is a plain exFAT volume whose root is the app folder, with 64 KiB clusters and the label `OVERDRIVE`. To release a new version, raise the version in `app/version.js` and `app/app.json`, run the workflow, test the draft's image on a console, then publish the draft: that creates its tag, and installed apps offer exactly the tested files on their next start.
Fixes over upstream ps5-react
Two fixes in the vendored framework, both in the build tooling and both reported by a Linux build: - `ps5-react/tools/common.py` read the `git apply --summary` line with a fixed space count, which glued the file mode onto the path (`100644 `) and made every fresh dependency checkout fail on the first patch that creates a file. It now splits on whitespace. - `ps5-react/tools/build_ps5.py` opened the pinned LLVM package's `data.tar.zst` with `tarfile`, which reads zstd only from Python 3.14 while the documented minimum is 3.12. It now falls back to the `zstd` command. Nothing else in the framework is changed.
## Credits - **[MyLuxy](https://github.com/MyLuxy)**, who decompiled Overdrive, recovered its source and rebuilt it. - **[ps5-react](https://github.com/half144/ps5-react)**, the framework it runs on. - **[ShadowMount+](https://github.com/drakmor/ShadowMountPlus)** by drakmor, which installs it. `ps5-react/` is GPL-3.0-or-later and carries its own `LICENSE`, `LICENSE-ATTRIBUTION` and `NOTICE`. Every dependency notice is copied into `notices/` inside the built app, and `ps5-react/docs/DEPENDENCIES.md` lists them with their sources. 事件防吞噬护盾、4px 移动死区、双击 50/50 吸附、边缘折叠门限与约束钳制。 * **[5.4 工件预览沙箱与隔离通信架构](docs/05-视听多媒体与产物交互物理学.md#54-工件预览沙箱与隔离通信架构)**：Epitaxy 隔离容器、7 大专有 MIME 分发、用户手势门禁与虚拟包重定向。 * **[5.5 items.name: gitdrive
items.description: Turn GitHub into an iCloud-style drive for macOS. Native Finder integration, files on demand, real git history, Git LFS, and optional ML-KEM + X25519 encryption where GitHub sees only random data.
items.readme:
GitDrive

Your private GitHub repos as a drive in Finder. Files download when you open them and can be removed from your Mac without leaving the cloud.

## Screenshots

 

## Features - **Lives in Finder.** GitDrive appears in the Finder sidebar like iCloud Drive or Dropbox, built on Apple's File Provider framework. - **Files on demand.** Everything is listed right away. A file downloads only when you open it. - **Frees up space.** Right-click and choose Remove Download, or use Free Up Space in the menu bar. macOS can also remove downloads on its own when the disk is low. - **Private by default.** Every top-level folder is its own private GitHub repo named `drive-`. - **Optional end-to-end encryption.** Post-quantum (ML-KEM-768 + X25519) with deduplication and compression. GitHub sees random data: no names, no folder layout, no file sizes. Needs macOS 26. See [docs/ENCRYPTION.md](docs/ENCRYPTION.md). - **Real git history.** Each save is a commit, so every old version stays recoverable on GitHub. - **Large files with Git LFS.** Optional: files over a size you choose go to Git LFS, up to 2 GB each. - **Keeps file dates.** Modification dates are saved in the repo, so every Mac shows the same dates. - **Works with other edits.** Changes made on github.com or from a clone show up in Finder within a minute. Edits on both sides keep both copies. - **Menu bar app.** Sync status, folder sizes, pause, launch at login. - **No local clones.** GitDrive talks to the GitHub API directly, so files are never stored twice. ### Extras Optional features, each with a switch in **Settings → Extras**: - **Finder:** Quick Look and thumbnails without downloading, search for files that aren't downloaded (including encrypted names), conflict badges. - **History:** Show Versions, Recently Deleted, a conflict viewer with side-by-side diff, a duplicate finder, a monthly bit-rot check. - **Safety:** Touch ID or a passcode for encrypted folders, decoy folders behind a duress passcode, a ransomware tripwire with one-hour rollback. - **Modes:** Photos (timeline, map, albums), Notes (Markdown with backlinks), daily versioned backups of Mac folders. - **GitHub:** publish a folder as a website, compress videos or make PDFs with GitHub Actions, open a folder in Codespaces. Details and defaults are in [docs/EXTRAS.md](docs/EXTRAS.md). ## How it works

The File Provider extension serves the drive to Finder. It keeps a small SQLite index of every file and folder, turns your edits into commits through the GitHub Git Data API, and pulls in remote changes by comparing trees. The menu bar app handles sign-in and asks the extension to check for changes every minute. More detail is in [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md). ## Install GitDrive is free and installs from source. You need macOS 14 or later, [Xcode](https://apps.apple.com/app/xcode/id497799835) (free), and an Apple ID added to Xcode under **Settings → Accounts**. A free Apple ID works; no paid developer account needed. ```bash git clone https://github.com/deeeeone/gitdrive.git cd gitdrive ./scripts/install.sh ``` The script installs XcodeGen if needed, finds your signing team, builds GitDrive, copies it to `/Applications` and opens it. It takes a minute or two the first time.
Building by hand instead ```bash brew install xcodegen cp Config/Local.xcconfig.example Config/Local.xcconfig ``` Set `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` and `GITDRIVE_BUNDLE_ID` in `Config/Local.xcconfig`, then: ```bash xcodegen generate open GitDrive.xcodeproj ``` Choose the **GitDrive** scheme and press Run.
> [!NOTE] > There are no prebuilt downloads. macOS only loads File Provider extensions from apps signed by a developer team, so each person builds GitDrive with their own Apple ID. Builds made this way run on the Mac that built them. ## First run 1. Click the cloud icon in the menu bar. 2. Sign in. Choose **Sign in with GitHub** (if the build has an OAuth Client ID), or paste a [personal access token](https://github.com/settings/tokens/new?scopes=repo,delete_repo&description=GitDrive) with the `repo` and `delete_repo` scopes. Without `delete_repo`, deleting a top-level folder fails unless you switch it to archive. 3. If macOS asks, turn on GitDrive in **System Settings → General → Login Items & Extensions → File Providers**. 4. Click **Open in Finder**. Make a folder at the top level and GitDrive creates a private repo for it. Already have repos you want in the drive? Open **Settings → Folders → Your other repos** and choose **Add to Drive**. ## Limits and fair use GitHub is built for source code, not as a general file host, so keep these in mind: | Limit | What happens | |---|---| | 100 MB per file | Turn on **Settings → General → Large files** to store bigger files with Git LFS, up to 2 GB each. | | Git LFS quota | GitHub Free includes 10 GiB of LFS storage and 10 GiB of downloads a month. Opening a file counts as a download. | | Repo size | GitHub recommends repos under 1 GB and strongly recommends under 5 GB. The menu bar warns past 1 GB. | | History | Deleted files still count toward repo size. **Settings → Folders → Compact History** keeps only the current files. | | API rate limit | 5,000 requests per hour. GitDrive uses conditional requests and backs off when it gets close. | | Top level | Each top-level item is a repo, so files go inside a folder, not at the very top. | Please read GitHub's [Acceptable Use Policies](https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/acceptable-use-policies/github-acceptable-use-policies) before storing large amounts of non-code data. ## Privacy and security - Your GitHub token is stored only in the macOS Keychain, shared between the app and its extension. - Repos GitDrive creates are always private. Turn on encryption and GitHub can't read them at all. - Your encryption key stays in iCloud Keychain. Each encrypted repo holds only the public key. - Deleting a top-level folder deletes its repo, after Finder asks. Choose **Settings → General → Top-level folders → Archives its GitHub repo** if you'd rather keep a read-only copy on GitHub. - Deleting anything else is a commit, so it can be recovered from the repo's history. - The only force-push is Compact History, which asks first. - No analytics, no telemetry, no servers other than GitHub. Found a security problem? See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ## Roadmap - [x] Git LFS for files over 100 MB - [x] Modification dates stored in the repo - [x] Moving folders between top-level folders - [x] End-to-end encryption with hidden file structure - [ ] Shared folders (repos you collaborate on) - [x] Decrypting a folder back to a readable repo - [x] Lock badge on encrypted folders in Finder - [ ] Signed and notarized release builds ## FAQ **Does it work offline?** Downloaded files open and save as usual. GitDrive uploads your changes when you are back online. **Can I use the repos with normal git?** Yes. They are ordinary repos. Clone them, push to them, and GitDrive picks up the changes. **What happens if I uninstall?** Nothing on GitHub changes. Sign out first to remove the downloaded copies from your Mac. **Why one repo per folder?** It keeps each repo small, lets you share or archive folders separately, and keeps the API traffic for one folder independent of the others. ## Contributing Contributions are welcome. Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for setup, code style and how to run the tests. Please follow the [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). ## License GitDrive is released under the [MIT License](LICENSE). ## Acknowledgements - [GRDB.swift](https://github.com/groue/GRDB.swift) for SQLite - [XcodeGen](https://github.com/yonaskolb/XcodeGen) for the project file - Apple's [File Provider](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/fileprovider) framework

items.name: graphicle
items.description: Code graph and memory for your coding agents, in one Rust program. For Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and any MCP client.
items.readme:
Code graph and memory for your coding agents, in one Rust program.

Graphicle maps your repository into a code graph, remembers your project's docs, decisions and past agent sessions, and gives your coding agent cited excerpts from both: the exact files and lines. It runs on your machine: no API key needed, no account, no telemetry.
Works with Claude Code · Cursor · Codex · VS Code · Claude Desktop · any MCP client

Quick start · How it works · Benchmarks · Docs · Coming from Graphify? · Discussions

## Quick start ```sh brew install graphicle-ai/tap/graphicle cd your-repo graphicle setup ``` No Homebrew? curl -fsSL https://github.com/graphicle-ai/graphicle/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh · [Release archives](https://github.com/graphicle-ai/graphicle/releases) · [Other ways to install](docs/install.md)
Windows: no native build yet; under WSL2 the Linux install should work (not yet tested). Native Windows support is planned. `graphicle setup` indexes the repository, builds its code graph and connects the coding agents it finds. It also turns on session capture, points Claude Code's searches to the code graph first, adds a short section to `AGENTS.md` and installs Git hooks that keep the project current. It lists every file it changes and backs each one up first; `graphicle disconnect` undoes it all. Then ask your agent to *"use graphicle to find where failed requests are retried"*, or ask from the terminal: ```console $ graphicle ask "where is tax added to prices?" Evidence for "where is tax added to prices?" 4 excerpts · 598 of 3,000 tokens [1] shop/pricing.py:1-7 price_with_tax() """Prices and tax.""" TAX_RATE = 0.2 def price_with_tax(price): """A price with the sales tax added.""" return round(price * (1 + TAX_RATE), 2) ``` Real output, cut after the first excerpt. With no model configured, ask shows the evidence; graphicle config set model anthropic (or openai, ollama) adds written answers.
Let your coding agent install it Paste this into Claude Code, Codex or Cursor: ```text Install Graphicle with `brew install graphicle-ai/tap/graphicle` (or, without Homebrew, `curl -fsSL https://github.com/graphicle-ai/graphicle/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh`), then run `graphicle setup --yes` in this repository and list every file it changed. ```
## Start here | You want to | Run | |---|---| | Give your coding agent the code graph and your project's memory | `graphicle setup` in the repository | | Ask a question from the terminal | `graphicle ask "how are failed requests retried?"` | | Browse the graph, the sources and the memory | `graphicle open` | | See what a change to a symbol touches | `graphicle graph extract . --code-only`, then `graphicle graph affected "retry()"` | | Check that everything works | `graphicle doctor` | | Undo everything setup did | `graphicle disconnect` | | Move from Graphify, or run a server for a team | [Moving from Graphify](docs/migrate-from-graphify.md) · [Team server](docs/team.md) | ## Why Graphicle - **Native and fast.** One Rust program. On Kubernetes (31k files), the 0.1.0 engine ran a code-only extract in 3 min 18 s, against 26 min 38 s for Graphify 0.9.88, and built the same graph (one exploratory run each, one Linux host, the same 16 CPUs, 8 workers). - **Context, not re-reading.** Your agent asks Graphicle and gets the relevant code, docs and decisions as cited excerpts, within a token budget. - **Answers you can check.** Every excerpt names its file and lines. Memories an agent proposes wait for your approval. - **One program, not a stack.** The code graph, the memory, one MCP server, the web app and the command line come in one install, with one SQLite file. No Python, Docker or database server. - **Local and private.** No account and no telemetry. Nothing leaves your machine unless you ask.

## What it does - **Code graph.** Files, functions, classes, calls and imports, parsed with tree-sitter and no model. `graphicle graph` searches it, explains a symbol, traces a path and exports an interactive HTML graph. After `graphicle graph extract . --code-only`, `graphicle graph affected "retry()"` lists what depends on a symbol. - **Project memory.** Docs (Markdown, PDF, Office, HTML), reviewed decisions and procedures, and past Claude Code and Codex sessions, searchable alongside the code. - **Cited context on a budget.** `graphicle context` and the MCP tools return excerpts with their sources, within a token budget, without calling a model. - **One MCP server.** `graphicle mcp` serves the code-graph tools, under Graphify's tool names such as `query_graph`, `get_neighbors` and `shortest_path`, next to the memory tools. - **Memory tied to your code.** Reviewed memories are tied to the functions they are about: a memory goes stale when that code changes, and edits elsewhere in the file usually leave it current ([the exact rule](crates/graphicle/README.md#memory-anchored-to-code-symbols)). Mentions of code in your docs are linked to the definitions they name (`graphicle call graph.doc_links` lists them). - **Across repositories.** Recall can span the repositories of a workspace: `graphicle context --workspace`, or [the workspace MCP endpoint](docs/mcp.md#several-projects-in-one-connection). - **Always current.** Before each answer Graphicle syncs the few files you changed; Git hooks sync after each commit, merge and checkout. - **No re-explaining.** Session capture keeps each finished turn, and each new session starts with your reviewed memories and the latest turns. - **An app.** `graphicle open` shows the graph, the sources and the memory in your browser. It is where you approve memories. ## Works with your agents `graphicle setup` connects every client it finds over MCP. Each file is backed up once as `.graphicle-bak`, and `graphicle disconnect` removes what it added. | Client | Where setup connects it | Session capture | |---|---|---| | Claude Code | `.mcp.json` in the repository | hooks in `.claude/settings.local.json` | | Codex | `~/.codex/config.toml` | hooks in `~/.codex/hooks.json` (Codex asks you to trust them) | | Cursor | `~/.cursor/mcp.json` | | | VS Code | `.vscode/mcp.json` in the repository | | | Claude Desktop | `claude_desktop_config.json` in Claude's settings folder | | | Any other MCP client | a short JSON entry ([MCP](docs/mcp.md)) | | ## How it works

1. **Sync.** Graphicle reads the folder (it respects `.gitignore` and skips secrets), keeps a versioned copy of each source and builds the code graph. 2. **Recall.** When your agent calls a tool, Graphicle syncs what changed, ranks excerpts from code, documents, sessions and reviewed memory, and returns them with citations. The tools call no model; your agent's own model reads the excerpts. 3. **Remember.** Captured sessions become sources. Memories that agents propose wait for your approval in the app. ## Graphicle, or a code-graph tool plus a memory server | | A code-graph tool + a memory server | Graphicle | |---|---|---| | Install | Two tools, often on different runtimes, and often a database server | One install | | Connect your agents | Configure each tool in each agent | `graphicle setup` connects the agents it finds; `graphicle disconnect` undoes it | | MCP servers in your agent | Two, configured separately | One, with the graph and the memory tools | | Storage | Graph files plus the memory server's database | One SQLite file in one data folder | | Code structure: calls, imports, impact | The graph tool | `graphicle graph` | | Docs, decisions, past sessions | The memory server | Built in | | Citations and review | Varies | A file and its lines on every excerpt; agent memories wait for approval | ## Benchmarks **Speed.** The chart above: Kubernetes (31k files), the 0.1.0 engine (a Linux test build of the release source) against Graphify 0.9.88, one exploratory run each, both building the same graph ([Kubernetes run](docs/benchmarks.md#speed-on-kubernetes)). Earlier, on Django, a pre-release build ran a code-only extract in 7.5 s against 72.8 s for Graphify 0.9.77 (medians of five alternating runs, one shared Linux host, 8 workers), both building the same graph ([the 8 October record](docs/benchmarks.md#speed-against-graphify-0977)). **Memory.** In a comparison with seven memory systems, registered before any answer was scored and run with one open model as every system's reader and judge, a pre-release build of Graphicle trails none on three development sets. [Every score, with its method and caveats](docs/benchmarks.md#agent-memory-comparison-with-seven-memory-systems). ## FAQ ### Privacy and local first - **One data folder.** Your sources, memories and the code graph that setup builds live in one SQLite store: `~/Library/Application Support/Graphicle` on macOS, `~/.local/share/graphicle` on Linux. `graphicle graph extract` writes its graph file to `.graphicle/` in the project. - **Loopback by default.** The app and its HTTP and MCP endpoints listen on 127.0.0.1. - **No telemetry, no account.** Graphicle connects to the network only when you ask it to: a model or a connector you configure, a full `graphicle graph extract` (it sends documents and images to the LLM whose API key it finds), the GitHub CLI for `graphicle graph add`, `clone` and the graph server's pull-request tools, and `graphicle update` with a feed you name. A build from source also downloads the parser sources once. [Details](docs/faq.md) - **Careful sync.** `sync` respects `.gitignore` and skips `.env` files, keys and credentials. Session capture drops `…` spans and redacts credentials. - **Forgetting with a receipt.** Deleting a memory or a captured session also removes what was derived from it, and you get a hash-chained deletion receipt.
Do I need an API key or a model? No, for most of it. The code graph (with `--code-only`), sync, `context`, the MCP server, session capture and the app work without one. A model writes the answers of `graphicle ask`, proposes memories from sources and reads documents and images in a full `graphicle graph extract`. Local models through Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible server work ([configuration](docs/configuration.md#models)).
Is Graphicle a fork of Graphify? The code-graph engine is a Rust port of Graphify, kept in step with Graphify's releases and credited in its file headers and in [NOTICE](NOTICE). [The parity checks](docs/benchmarks.md#parity-with-graphify) name the release it follows. The memory, the memory tools, the app and session capture are not part of Graphify. Coming from Graphify? `graphicle setup` offers to switch a repository, backs up each file and never deletes `graphify-out/` ([Moving from Graphify](docs/migrate-from-graphify.md)).
Will it handle my large repository? By default a project can hold up to 100,000 text files and 1 GiB of text; you can raise both (see [Limits in docs/configuration.md](docs/configuration.md#limits)). A very large file is analysed in part or kept as searchable text instead of stopping a sync.
Is there a version for teams? Graphicle is free and open source under Apache-2.0, for individuals and teams alike. A commercial edition for teams is in private preview. To talk to us, start a discussion: https://github.com/graphicle-ai/graphicle/discussions, or chat with us on [Discord](https://discord.com/invite/rWuU7cWU4E).
What is the licence? Graphicle is Apache-2.0: free to use, change and ship, commercially too. Third-party parts keep their own licences, listed in [NOTICE](NOTICE).
More answers: [FAQ](docs/faq.md) · [Troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md) · or run `graphicle doctor`. ## Documentation [Quick start](docs/quickstart.md) · [Agents](docs/agents.md) · [MCP](docs/mcp.md) · [Install](docs/install.md) · [Configuration](docs/configuration.md) · [Team server](docs/team.md) · [Moving from Graphify](docs/migrate-from-graphify.md) · [Benchmarks](docs/benchmarks.md) · [FAQ](docs/faq.md) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) The code: [`crates/graphicle/`](crates/graphicle/README.md) (the program: command line, app, HTTP and MCP server), [`crates/graphicle-graph/`](crates/graphicle-graph/README.md) (the code-graph engine), [`crates/graphicle-memory/`](crates/graphicle-memory/README.md) (the memory library), SDKs for [Python](sdk/python/README.md) and [TypeScript](sdk/typescript/README.md), and a team server recipe in [`deploy/`](deploy/README.md). Each crate builds on its own ([building from source](docs/install.md)). ## Contributing Contributions are welcome under the Apache License 2.0, with a Developer Certificate of Origin sign-off (`git commit -s`) and no CLA. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). To report a security problem, follow [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) rather than opening a public issue. ## License and credits Graphicle is licensed under the [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE). Copyright 2026 KarLex AI, Inc. The code-graph engine is a Rust port of [Graphify](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify) by Safi Shamsi and the Graphify contributors, licensed under Apache-2.0, with portions that remain available under the MIT License. Thank you. [NOTICE](NOTICE), [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md) and the `licenses/` folders hold the attributions and the licences of every adapted project and third-party component.

items.readme:
# Claudemy: an open-source alternative to Udemy and Coursera

![Claudemy: any topic, researched into 2-minute audio lessons](.github/social-preview.png)

**Claudemy is a free Claude Code skill that turns any topic into a short audio course.** You type what you want to learn. Claude researches it on the web, works out what good sources agree on, and builds a set of 2-minute lessons: two voices talking, a one-screen card, and one small thing to try. Every lesson links to the pages it came from.

```
> teach me negotiation
```

No catalog, no subscription, no 40-hour video course. Learn exactly the topic you need, at your level, in lessons short enough to finish.

## What you get
- **About 12 audio lessons, 2 minutes each.** Two hosts talking, not a lecture. MP3 files you can play anywhere.
- **A card per lesson:** the idea in three lines, how many sources agree (and who disagrees), one small practice, and links to go deeper.
- **A playbook:** one rule per lesson, collected in one file you keep.
- **A lesson plan** that shows where the experts split, laid out as decisions rather than lessons.
- **Real citations.** A checker refuses any lesson that cites a page the research didn't actually read.

## How it works
1. **Maps the topic** into sub-topics, from how it's usually taught.
2. **Researches the web:** 20 to 40 pages from practitioners, official docs, research summaries and a few dissenting views. No more than 3 pages from one site, so no single voice dominates.
3. **Reads and compares:** reader agents pull cited notes, then one agent merges them into themes with agreement counts.
4. **Plans the course** in arcs of about 4 lessons, foundations first.
5. **Makes one sample lesson** and waits for your reaction, then writes and records the rest.

Want a class built from one person's work instead? Say so: `teach me negotiation from <name>'s writing`. It reads their Substack or blog and builds the class from that.

## Install
As a Claude Code plugin:
```
/plugin marketplace add assafkip/claudemy
/plugin install claudemy@claudemy
```
Or copy `skills/claudemy/` into `~/.claude/skills/`, or download [`dist/claudemy.skill`](dist/claudemy.skill).

## Needs
- [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) with web search.
- Python 3 with `beautifulsoup4` (`pip install beautifulsoup4`), and `ffmpeg`.
- Audio: an ElevenLabs API key in `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` for natural two-voice lessons. Without one, macOS's built-in voices are used (free, plainer).
- Optional: `pandoc` for a Word copy of the cards.

Voices can be changed with `CLAUDEMY_VOICE_A` / `CLAUDEMY_VOICE_B` (ElevenLabs voice ids) or `CLAUDEMY_SAY_A` / `CLAUDEMY_SAY_B` (macOS voices).

## FAQ

**Is Claudemy free?**
Yes. The skill is MIT licensed. You pay only for what you already use: your Claude plan, and ElevenLabs credits if you want the premium voices. The macOS voices cost nothing.

**How is it different from Udemy or Coursera?**
Course sites sell a fixed course someone recorded once. Claudemy builds a course on the topic you name, at your level, from current sources, and shows you where those sources disagree. Lessons are 2 minutes and end in one thing to try, so the course is built to be finished.

**What topics does it work for?**
Anything people write about well on the open web: skills (negotiation, public speaking, sourdough), professional topics (pricing, hiring, SQL), and subjects (stoicism, music theory). Health, legal and financial topics get a note where advice depends on your situation.

**Does it copy other people's content?**
No. It reads pages the way a researcher does, writes its own lessons, and links to the sources. Pages it reads are saved only in your local workspace for your own study.

**Can I use it without ElevenLabs?**
Yes. On a Mac it falls back to the built-in voices. The cards and playbook work with no audio at all.

**How long does a course take to make?**
A 12-lesson course is a long-running Claude Code session: research, reading, writing and about 25 minutes of generated audio.

**Can I learn from one specific expert?**
Yes. Name them in the request. Claudemy finds their Substack or blog and builds the course from their writing.

## License
MIT. Free to use, change and share.

items.description: trim-1: a 1.2 MB model that keeps the lines of a context an AI agent needs
items.readme: # trim-1 trim-1 is a small model that decides which lines of a context an AI agent needs for its current ask, and drops the rest. Give it a context (a tool result, a file, a log, a long chat) and the current query. It returns the context's own lines, in their original order, with a short marker wherever lines were removed. It never rewrites or summarizes a line, so identifiers, paths and error text come through exactly as they were. - **1.2 MB.** 712 gradient-boosted trees, not a neural network. - **Milliseconds on one CPU core.** No GPU, no network call. - **Deterministic.** No sampling and no randomness: the same context and query give the same output. - **No dependencies.** Pure Go, standard library only. The model is embedded. The model card, with benchmark results and limits, is on Hugging Face: [caveman-so/trim-1](https://huggingface.co/caveman-so/trim-1). ## Install Needs Go 1.23 or newer. ```bash go install github.com/caveman-ai/trim-1/cmd/trim@latest ``` ## Use From the command line: ```bash trim --query "why does the build fail" build.log > build.trimmed.log ``` ```bash cat long-document.md | trim --query "what is the refund policy" --point balanced ``` The trimmed context goes to stdout. A one-line summary goes to stderr: ``` trim: kept 246 lines, removed 189, 47831 -> 36344 bytes ``` From Go: ```go import trim "github.com/caveman-ai/trim-1" res := trim.Compress(context, query, trim.Options{Point: "balanced"}) fmt.Print(res.Output) ``` `trim.Score(context, query)` returns every line with its keep probability, if you want to make the selection yourself. ## Which setting to use `--point` decides how hard trim-1 cuts: `conservative`, `balanced` (the default) or `aggressive`. Cutting harder costs quality, because every removed line is one the model can no longer read. - **Long-document retrieval** is what trim-1 is for. Use `balanced`. - **Coding-agent tool outputs** are short and dense. Stay at `balanced` or `conservative` and expect small savings. The [model card](https://huggingface.co/caveman-so/trim-1#which-setting-to-use) has the numbers behind this. ## When it does nothing trim-1 fails closed. It returns the context unchanged, and says why on stderr, when: - the query is blank, - the context is under 2,000 bytes, - the context is over 8 MiB or 200,000 lines, - the context already has a removal marker line, such as trim-1's own output, - the cut would remove less than 10% of the bytes. The `trim` command exits with status 2 on a missing `--query` or an unknown `--point`. Flags go before the file name. ## Test ```bash go test ./... ``` `TestPredictionParity` checks the Go tree evaluation against the training library's own predictions, bit for bit. `TestGolden` pins the full output on a sample log. ## License Apache-2.0. `model.go` includes a copy of Go's `math.Exp`, under the BSD license in `LICENSE-go`. trim-1 is the model inside [Caveman](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman).

# Capivara Bet

![Capivara Bet — casino lobby (screenshot)](docs/images/capivara-bet-casino-screenshot.jpg)

**Capivara Bet** is a white-label **casino and sportsbook platform** built on the [Script.Casino](https://script.casino) / VanguardLTE stack: player lobby, wallet, admin back office, bonuses, reporting, and game catalogue integration.

This repository contains the **application source**, Docker setup, and operator documentation for self-hosted deployments.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Product** | Capivara Bet |
| **Platform** | [Script.Casino](https://script.casino) |
| **Stack** | Laravel 8 · PHP 7.4 · MariaDB · React player shell · optional Node sports ingestion |
| **Try it** | Self-host with Docker → http://127.0.0.1:8080 |

---

## Overview

Use this repo to **evaluate, brand, and deploy** your own Capivara Bet instance. The lobby, sports views, and admin tools ship here; **you** provide hosting, compliance, payment configuration, and **licensed game client assets** where required.

**This repository does not operate a casino.** It does not accept wagers, process real-money payments, or grant gambling licences. Running it locally is a **software demo** on your machine only.

---

## Key features

- **Player front office** — casino grid, categories, providers, sports navigation, wallet UI (gateways configured in admin).
- **Back office** — shops, users, roles, games, bonuses, tournaments, statistics.
- **Sports** — Laravel sports API + optional **Node ingestion** (port `1213`) when `SPORTS_API_TOKEN` is set.
- **Docker** — MariaDB seed schema, web container, optional sports service.
- **Branding** — Capivara Bet theme (logo, copy, footer); adaptable for your operator brand.

---

## What is in this repo vs what you add

| Included in GitHub | Not included (by design) |
|--------------------|---------------------------|
| Laravel / VanguardLTE application code | Third-party **slot HTML5 client packs** (`public/games/…`) |
| Database seed / schema for local dev | Studio trademarks & artwork you are not licensed to redistribute |
| Compiled front-end (`public/js`, themes) | Production secrets (`.env`, keys, payment credentials) |
| GeoIP path docs under `storage/app/GeoIP2-City_20201006/` | **MaxMind `GeoIP2-City.mmdb`** (~127 MB — download locally) |
| Server-side game logic under `app/Games/` | Guarantee of playable slots without your licensed asset mount |

**Playable slots** need client files on disk or `GAME_ASSETS_PATH` pointing at your licensed bundle — the same class of requirement as templates that sell a separate “games API” or asset pack. The lobby lists games from the database; the browser loads the client from `public/games/{GameName}/`.

---

## Quick start (self-hosted)

**Requirements:** Docker Engine 24+ and Docker Compose v2.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/evascasino/Capivara_casino.git
cd Capivara_casino
cp .env.example .env
docker compose up --build -d
```

| Service | URL |
|---------|-----|
| Web | http://127.0.0.1:8080 |
| Sports ingestion (optional) | http://127.0.0.1:1213/health |

First boot waits for MariaDB, syncs Compose env into `.env`, and generates `APP_KEY` if missing.

**Reset database:**

```bash
docker compose down -v && docker compose up --build -d
```

**Optional — mount licensed game clients:**

```bash
# .env
GAME_ASSETS_PATH=/absolute/path/to/your/games
# or copy bundles into public/games/
```

---

## Configuration

| Variable | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `APP_URL` | Public URL of your deployment |
| `DB_*` | MariaDB connection (`DB_PREFIX` default `w_`) |
| `JWT_SECRET` | API tokens — long random value in production |
| `GAME_ASSETS_PATH` | Optional path to licensed slot client packs |
| `SPORTS_API_TOKEN` | External odds feed (empty = sports UI without ingestion) |

Payment, SMS, and crypto modules: **Admin → Settings** and `.env.example`.

---

## Development without Docker

```bash
composer install
cp .env.example .env
php artisan key:generate
# Import docker/01-schema.sql, then:
php artisan serve
```

---

## Repository layout

```
app/                 Laravel application (VanguardLTE namespace)
docker/              DB seed, sports Dockerfile
public/              Web root (themes, compiled JS; games/ when you add assets)
resources/views/     Blade templates (Default theme)
sports/              Node sports ingestion service
routes/              Web + API routes
```

---

## Support

- **Issues:** [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/evascasino/Capivara_casino/issues) for bugs and integration questions.
- **Platform:** [Script.Casino](https://script.casino)

Operators are responsible for compliance with applicable laws and licences in their jurisdictions.

---

## Licence
